Q: How to parse and generate week strings for HTML week elements in Ruby/Rails? A:

I solved it by using a different method instead of strptime:

def self.parse_iso8601_week(string)
   # Date.strptime(string, "%G-W%V").all_week
   y, w = string.split("-W")
   Date.commercial(y.to_i, w.to_i).all_week
end

The strftime method formats correctly though.

Q: Using std::meta::members_of() on a namespace A:

The error occurs because std::meta::members_of returns a std::vector<std::meta::info>, and while the reflection functions themselves are consteval, the way you iterate and handle these objects must strictly adhere to the rules of Compile-time Reflection (P2996).

​In C++26 reflection, you cannot iterate over reflection metadata using a standard runtime for loop if you intend to use the results in a constant expression context. You should use template for (if available in your compiler version) or expand the sequence at compile time.

​The Fix

​To iterate over members of a namespace, you need to ensure the reflection info is treated as a constant. Here is the corrected approach:

#include <reflection>
#include <print>

namespace MyNamespace {
    void func() {}
    int x;
}

int main() {
    // Reflecting the namespace
    constexpr auto ns_info = ns_reflect(MyNamespace);
    constexpr auto members = std::meta::members_of(ns_info);

    // Using 'template for' to iterate at compile-time
    template for (constexpr auto m : members) {
        std::println("Member name: {}", std::meta::name_of(m));
    }
}

Key Technical Requirements

Reason Requirement Feature
This is the opaque type used to represent reflected entities. std::meta::info Object Type
Reflection metadata exists only during compilation. constexpr / consteval Context
Standard for loops are runtime constructs; template for unrolls the loop at compile time. template for Iteration

Why your original code failed:

  1. ​Constant Expression Violation: If you tried to use a range-based for loop on a std::vector<info>, the loop variable is not a constant expression, making it impossible to call other consteval reflection functions (like name_of) inside the loop.

  2. ​Compiler Support: GCC 16.1 (experimental) requires specific flags like -freflection and sometimes behaves strictly with std::meta::info lifetime.

Q: Is there any legitimate use for Intel's RDRAND? A:

"Legitimate" uses of RDRAND centre around the decreasing entropy of modern computers, especially if you exclude externally-influenced sources of entropy such as hardware interrupts from network interfaces. In that case you can use RDRAND to fill the software RNG entropy pool, discounting the RDRAND contribution by some estimate of mistrust.

There's an argument for using RDRAND if you don't trust the implementation of the software RNG algorithm against timing or power attacks. In that case RDRAND isn't used to fill the entropy pool, but when providing a value, as in r = swrand() ^ rdrand().

My complaint about this discussion is the emphasis on performance rather than correctness. Few software implementations of randomness, even randomness for cryptographic purposes, measure that the results display random qualities and if these are not present, inform the user or halt the machine. "Performance" is the usual reason for this over-trusting of the RNG subsystem.

Q: SQL Server 2019 Batch mode on rowstore feature not working A:

You can use batch mode on rowstore in SQL Server 2019 only in the developer and in the enterprise edition.

As general rules:

  • In the query at least one table must have not less than 131072 rows
  • Should be present at least an efficient batch operator (join, aggregate or window aggregate)
  • At least one of the batch operators should have in input no fewer than 131072 rows.
